name: Secular humanism
summary: Secular humanism holds that ethics and knowledge rest on human reason, evidence and experience rather than on divine authority, and that society should be organised around free inquiry, human rights and democracy. Politically it demands strict separation of church and state and of ideology and state, civil liberties, participatory democracy and an open society, opposes every form of totalitarianism, supports reproductive and sexual freedom, equality without discrimination, a world community with international law, and treats economic systems as tools to be judged by results.
scope: Secular humanism as the Council for Secular Humanism and Paul Kurtz define it: A Secular Humanist Declaration (1980), the Affirmations of Humanism and the Council's own definition, with the American Humanist Association's Humanist Manifesto II (1973), which Kurtz co-wrote and which the Declaration grew from, as its predecessor text. It excludes religious humanism, Renaissance humanism and atheism as such; the Declaration itself says views that merely reject theism are not equivalent to humanism.
